messages:
pagerduty-bot: ALERT: High error rate on staging-auth (svc-auth-proxy). 2.3k 401s in 3m, unusual token reuse patterns. Possible leaked staging tokens. Paging on-call.

devon: on it, taking lead for triage. tagging @anya for sec assist.

anya: thanks — can you paste recent nginx access logs sample? looking for same token/ua/ip combos.

devon: grabbing tail now. snippet:
```
10.142.12.8 - - [15/Mar/2026:15:02:12 +0000] "POST /v1/auth HTTP/1.1" 401 45 "-" "svc-agent/1.2" token=stg_xxxabc123 same_id=abcd
10.142.12.8 - - [15/Mar/2026:15:02:13 +0000] "POST /v1/auth HTTP/1.1" 200 512 "-" "svc-agent/1.2" token=stg_xxxabc123 same_id=abcd
```

anya: weird — same token showing both 401 and 200 from different IPs. looks like token replay from multiple sources.

sarah: also noticed an increase in our log-forwarder retry errors to third-party syslog forwarder at ~15:00. Could be correlated.

owen: I see a spike in SQS retries on the staging-log-forwarder queue, messages containing `staging-agent` debug dumps. Pulling sample.

devon: priority: 1) stop log-forwarding out of staging, 2) revoke staging service tokens, 3) block suspicious IPs, 4) assess customer exposure. who can flip the log forwarder?

infra-bot: `ops-runbook/staging/log-forwarder` flagged. toggle endpoint: POST /ops/toggle-forwarder?env=staging (requires ops token).

jules-cs: we have one external partner that uses staging tenants for validation. need an immediate customer-impact check if their data might be in forwarded logs.

devon: @infra-bot — can you cut the staging -> external syslog subscription now?

infra-bot: done. staging-log-forwarder subscription disabled (action id: act-9f3). confirmation: 15:05 UTC. :white_check_mark:

anya: good. next, rotate all staging service tokens and short-lived creds. I'll coordinate with devon for the revoke commands.

devon: running rotation script:
```
rdrctl auth list --env=staging --filter=service:staging-agent | jq '.[] | .token_id' | xargs -n1 -I{} rdrctl auth revoke --id {}
```
Started at 15:06. Expect revokes to complete in ~30s.

audit-bot: detected 12 token revocations in staging by devon (cmd-run). logging to secure-audit (audit-id: A-20260315-176432).

anya: while revoking, put temporary IP block for 10.0.0.0/8? suspiciouss showed internal-like address range from probes. Better to block the CIDR range we confirmed to be bad: 35.190.220.0/24 and 52.34.10.0/24 for now.

devon: Pushing WAF rules and security group deny for those CIDRs.
```
aws wafv2 update-ip-set --name "staging-threat-ipset" --scope REGIONAL --addresses "[\"35.190.220.0/24\", \"52.34.10.0/24\"]"
```
Applied at 15:08.

sarah: quick forensics note — preserve current forwarder queue and a copy of all forwarded payloads, we might need them for legal and root cause. @legal-ops FYI.

legal-ops: acknowledged. preserve and export to secure-share. do not share externally. we need to know if any customer PII hit the forwarder.

jules-cs: checking customers that touched staging in last 24h. hitting our lookup now. will post list in ~10.

anya: also enable increased auth logging with masked tokens for the next 2h to collect replay patterns. Use `mask=last4` rule.

devon: done. enhanced logs enabled at 15:10.

jules-cs: customers with staging tenants showing forwarded logs: partner-acme, partner-beta. both are internal test tenants but partner-acme had some sample customer emails in logs (masked). Creating CS ticket to notify partners as a precaution.

jules-cs: CS ticket created: CS-7891. Recommended wording drafted, flagging as "informational - possible staging exposure".

anya: triage severity: S2 (staging credential exposure with limited external forwarding). Timeline: detection 15:02, forwarder cut 15:05, revokes started 15:06, WAF block 15:08, enhanced logging 15:10.

devon: outstanding actions: 1) complete full token rotation and validate no remaining valid staging tokens; 2) confirm no long-lived creds in logs; 3) rotate any CI/CD credentials that reference staging-agent; 4) follow-up forensic export; 5) CS and legal notification.

sarah: I'll scope CI/CD secrets scanning run now (starting) and report any matches.

anya: good. nominate follow-up owners: devon (mitigation + rotation), sarah (forensics + secrets scanning), jules-cs (customer comms), legal-ops (compliance). check back in 30.

devon: rotation finished at 15:18. `rdrctl auth status --env=staging` shows 0 active service tokens for staging-agent.

audit-bot: revocation batch complete (12 tokens), scan id A-20260315-176432.

sarah: initial secrets scan found 1 pipeline job referencing `staging-agent` as env var in repo infra/ci (job-id: 452). I've opened PR to remove and rotate those creds.

jules-cs: CS notifications sent to partner-acme and partner-beta at 15:22 with mitigation steps and invite for follow-up call.

legal-ops: will prepare formal incident memo if forensics shows customer PII in forwarded logs. hold on public comms until we confirm.

anya: thanks team. keep thread updated. we'll do a short post-incident review tomorrow 10:30 UTC.

devon: recap and checklist I will append to the incident ticket. closing active mitigation, leaving incident as monitored (S2).

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged closed by devon. Monitoring continues.
